problem.title: Connection problem · {{name}}
problem.ipFromServer: The server says you connected from {{ip}} (unverified: “See my public IP” confirms it).

firewall.title: The server's firewall blocks your IP
firewall.azure: Azure SQL only accepts connections from the IPs allowed in the server's firewall, and yours isn't one of them. Add it as a rule and connect again (the change can take a few minutes).
firewall.other: The server doesn't accept connections from your address. Ask for your public IP to be allowed (for example in pg_hba.conf, the MySQL user's allowed hosts or the server's firewall).

timeout.title: The server didn't answer
timeout.body: The connection didn't reach the server in time. Most often:

refused.title: The server refused the connection
refused.body: The machine was reached but nothing is listening on that port, or there's no route to it. Most often:

dns.title: The server can't be found
dns.body: The name {{host}} doesn't resolve. Check that it's spelled right and, if it's an internal name, that you're on the network or VPN that resolves it.

tls.title: The secure connection (TLS) failed
tls.body: The server's certificate isn't trusted or doesn't match the host name. Check the connection's encryption options: use the name on the certificate, or trust the server's certificate only if you know it's the right one.

tls_not_offered.title: The server doesn't offer TLS
tls_not_offered.body: The connection asks for encryption and the server doesn't have it turned on (common on development servers). Turn TLS on in the server or, if you accept that the data and the password travel unencrypted, choose a mode without encryption in the SSL/TLS tab.

tls_untrusted.title: The server's certificate couldn't be verified
tls_untrusted.body: The server's certificate isn't signed by a trusted authority or doesn't match the host name (common with self-signed certificates). In the SSL/TLS tab, set the CA file or, only if you know the server is the right one, choose a mode that doesn't verify the certificate.

auth.title: Login rejected
auth.body: The server rejected the user or password. Check the credentials and the authentication method (for example Microsoft Entra), and that the user exists in that database.

unknown.title: Couldn't connect
unknown.body: The server or the driver answered with this message.

network.vpn: The VPN to the server's network isn't connected.
network.firewall: A firewall on the way (an Azure NSG or WAF, the virtual machine's firewall or your network's) drops traffic to port {{port}}.
network.down: The server or the service is stopped, or listens on another port.
network.azureVm: {{host}} is an Azure virtual machine: SQL Server runs on the VM, so the rule goes in its NSG or WAF (or the VM's Windows firewall), not in the Azure SQL firewall.
network.azureSql: With Azure SQL, an IP that isn't allowed gets a firewall error, not a timeout: if it doesn't answer, check that your network lets port 1433 out.

azure.byTsql: With T-SQL, from another connection that does have access, in the master database:

help.command: Runs with your login shell, with no input and for 30 s at most; what it prints (without the trailing newline) is the secret.
help.json_key: If the secret is a JSON object, the key to use.
help.onepassword: Read with the 1Password CLI («op read»): it must be installed and signed in.
help.vault: Without a token, VAULT_TOKEN or the one from «vault login» (~/.vault-token) is used. The token you type is saved in the system keychain.
help.aws: Uses this computer's AWS credentials: environment variables, ~/.aws or the AWS CLI (SSO, roles).
help.azure: Uses your Azure CLI session («az login»), Azure Developer CLI or the managed identity.
help.gcp: Uses your gcloud session («gcloud auth login») or the application default credentials.
help.entry: Group/Subgroup/Title, the title alone if it isn't repeated, or the entry's UUID.
help.keepass: The database is read on this computer, with no external programs (KDBX 3.1 and 4). The master password you type is saved in the system keychain; with «Ask when connecting» it is asked the first time you connect and stays in memory only until you close DBine.
help.zoho: With your own client («Self Client») from the Zoho API console and a refresh token with the ZohoVault.secrets.READ and ZohoVault.user.READ scopes. Values are decrypted on this computer with the master passphrase; the client secret, the token and the passphrase you type are saved in the system keychain.
help.vault_db: Vault creates a user and a password for this connection with the database engine (or gives those of a static role), and the connection's user is taken from there. The credentials are reused while the connection is open, renewed before they expire and revoked when you disconnect or close DBine. Without a token, VAULT_TOKEN or the one from «vault login» is used.
help.approle: DBine signs in with AppRole (auth/<path>/login) and revokes that token when it finishes. The secret ID you type is saved in the system keychain.
help.conjur: Uses the API key of a Conjur host or user, which is saved in the system keychain. Conjur Cloud: https://<subdomain>.secretsmgr.cyberark.cloud/api and the account «conjur». HTTPS only (HTTP only for this computer).
help.ccp: Requests the account from CyberArk's Central Credential Provider (AIMWebService) with the AppID and, if the provider requires it, a client certificate: PEM (with the key in the same file or in a separate one) or PKCS#12 (.p12/.pfx). The passphrase you type is saved in the system keychain. HTTPS only.
help.delinea: Signs in to Secret Server with OAuth2 (a user or an application account) and reads the secret's field by its slug. With Delinea Platform, the token is requested from the tenant (https://<tenant>.delinea.app) with the ID and secret of a service user. The secret's ID or name: if more than one has that name, use the ID. HTTPS only.
help.server: bitwarden.com, bitwarden.eu or the URL of your own server (https://; http:// only on this computer).
help.bitwarden: With a personal API key (Account settings › Security › Keys: client_id and client_secret). The vault is decrypted on this computer with the master password, with no external programs. Field: password, username, notes or the name of a custom field; if the value is JSON (for example, the notes), give its key. The client_secret and the password you type are saved in the system keychain.
help.bitwarden_sm: With the access token of a machine account; the secret is decrypted on this computer. Without a token, BWS_ACCESS_TOKEN is used. The token you type is saved in the system keychain.
help.ssm: With this computer's AWS credentials, like AWS Secrets Manager. SecureString is decrypted (kms:Decrypt is required); for a StringList, the item you indicate is used (1 is the first).
